nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Structural normative models were estimated using warped Bayesian Linear Regression (WBLR) on approximately 58,000 subjects. Functional normative models used Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) with likelihood warping (sinarcsinsh warping function, equivalent to SHASH distribution) on approximately 22,000 subjects. Both used B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with 5 evenly spaced knots) for non-linear age effects. Site variation was modeled using fixed effects. Hyperparameters were optimized using Powell algorithm. PCNtoolkit (version 0.26) was used.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: For the structural data, we used a publicly shared repository of pre-trained normative models that were estimated on approximately 58,000 subjects using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression algorithm; In addition to normative models of brain structure, we also expanded our repository by estimating normative models of brain functional connectivity (resting-state brain networks, Yeo-17 and Smith-10) using the same algorithm (Bayesian Linear Regression) as the structural models; Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) with likelihood warping was used to predict each Yeo-17 network pair from a vector of covariates (age, sex, mean_FD, site)
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Rutherford2023.pdf.md: Normative model formulation section; Appendix 1 - Functional Brain Networks Normative Modeling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Structural MRI: Cortical thickness and subcortical volume extracted using Freesurfer recon-all pipeline from Destrieux atlas (aparc) and Freesurfer subcortical atlas (aseg). Surface area models were also shared. Functional MRI: Between-network connectivity (136 unique network pairs) from Yeo-17 atlas and Smith-10 ICA-based parcellation. Connectivity matrices calculated using full correlation with Fisher r-to-z transformation.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For structural MRI, this corresponds to the cortical thickness files that are output after running the Freesurfer recon-all pipeline. We used the aparcstats2table and asegstats2table functions to extract the cortical thickness and subcortical volume from each region in the Destrieux atlas and Freesurfer subcortical atlas; Normative models of surface area were also added to the same repository; Large-scale brain networks from the 17-network Yeo atlas were then extracted and between-network connectivity was calculated using full correlation

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Structural models: age (with B-spline basis expansion - cubic spline with 5 evenly spaced knots for non-linear effects), sex, site (fixed effects), and Euler number (data quality metric from Freesurfer). Functional models: age (same B-spline approach), sex, site (fixed effects), and mean framewise displacement (data quality metric). Site variation was modeled using fixed effects in both cases.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The covariates used to train the structural normative models included age, sex, data quality metric (Euler number), and site; The covariates used to train the functional normative models were similar to the structural normative models which included age, sex, data quality metric (mean framewise displacement), and site; Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) with likelihood warping was used to predict each Yeo-17 network pair from a vector of covariates (age, sex, mean_FD, site); consisting of a B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with 5 evenly spaced knots) to model non-linear effects of age
